off.label: Explanations by template
off.summary: No language model is configured, so explanations are written from fixed templates.

rejected.label: Model output refused
rejected.summary: The model is answering, and its sentences are being refused because they contain figures that are not in the evidence.

unknown.label: Not recorded

unknown.consequence: Observations written before this was tracked do not say who wrote them, and are shown as they are rather than guessed at.

fund.title: Fund the model — about $0.45 a month
fund.detailFree: Measured from real usage: roughly $0.0015 per explanation, and about ten new findings a day. A capable model restates the evidence without deriving figures of its own, which is what the free one cannot do.
fund.detailPaid: Measured from real usage: roughly $0.0015 per explanation, and about ten new findings a day. The figure moves with how much the holdings move.

templates.title: Stay on templates — no cost, no change needed
templates.detail: Fixed phrasing over the same checked figures. Nothing is ever wrong and nothing is ever invented; what is lost is prose that can describe an unusual finding in its own words rather than in a sentence written in advance.

targets.title: Target weights
targets.intro: A target is your own statement of the share of the portfolio you meant to hold in something. It is the only thing the drift rule compares against: with no targets set, nothing here can drift, and the portfolio is only ever described rather than measured against an intention. Targets need not add up to 100% — covering three of your holdings is a normal thing to do, and the rest is simply not spoken for.
targets.emptyTitle: Nothing to set a target on
targets.emptyBody: A target names an instrument this portfolio already knows. Add a holding or import a file first, and every symbol in it becomes a row here.
targets.unpriced_one: No drift will be reported while {{symbols}} is unpriced. Every weight is a share of the whole portfolio, so leaving a holding out of the total would overstate all the others and invent a drift that is not there. The engine skips the rule entirely rather than report weights it knows are wrong.
targets.unpriced_other: No drift will be reported while {{symbols}} are unpriced. Every weight is a share of the whole portfolio, so leaving a holding out of the total would overstate all the others and invent a drift that is not there. The engine skips the rule entirely rather than report weights it knows are wrong.
targets.explainer: Leave a box empty for no target at all — that instrument is then never compared against anything. A target of <num>0</num> is a different statement: it means you meant to hold none of it, and everything you still hold counts as drift. Drift is reported once it reaches {{info}} percentage points, and is called high at {{high}}.
targets.unsaved: Unsaved changes. Nothing is compared against these until you save.
targets.savedNextScan: Saved. Drift is measured on the next scan, not immediately.
targets.portfolioMissing: The portfolio has not loaded, so the current weights are unknown and no drift is shown. The targets themselves are unaffected.
targets.notHeld: not held — the intention is kept, and holding none of it is itself the drift

topicsPage.title: Topics
topicsPage.intro: A topic is a theme you want to follow, in your own words: “uranium”, “robot surgery”. Type one and the app suggests instruments whose business descriptions are about it, each with the sentence that matched. Suggestions are never ticked for you, and you can add any ticker they missed. Following a topic buys nothing; it decides what the app watches.
